newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Canberra drops some price surveillance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Canberra drops some price surveillance.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Thursday the government would restrict prices surveillance to industries with insufficient competition.

"The government will retain the Prices Surveillance Act, but in future, prices surveillance will only be applied in those markets where competitive pressures are not sufficient to achieve efficient prices and protect consumers," Costello said in a statement.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and industry groups would monitor prices and advise the government if competition did not keep prices down, he said.
-- Beer and cigarettes, with a condition that prices rises be kept below the general inflation rate for the next year; and
-- Steel mill products supplied by The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd.
-- Wine bottles and glass food containers (300 ml to 600ml) produced by ACI Operations, a unit of BTR Plc, although other ACI products would be no longer subject to surveillance.
Surveillance was being considered for petrol pricing, with the government writing to motoring organisations encouraging petrol price monitoring in country areas, Costello said.
The Liberal-National government endorsed wider access to oil company terminals, saying more competition generated by this move would make price deregulation feasible.
It also encouraged state, territory and local governments to remove anti-competitive legislation restricting trading of retail fuel outlets.
